threshold: Pre-registered in round18/L1-toolchain/PREREG.md before any run. (a) EXACT IJG QUALITY asserted only if interval-arithmetic inversion over libjpeg's temp=(base*scale+50)/100 rule admits exactly one integer quality consistent with all 64 luma AND all 64 chroma coefficients, and PC1 recovers 6/6 planted qualities. (b) ENCODER NAMED only if a control pipeline reproduces byte-identical DQT tables + identical Huffman-table classification + identical subsampling + identical component-count behaviour; anything less is written as 'consistent with'. (c) YEAR BOUND asserted only from a dated artefact inside the file, quoted verbatim. (d) FONT IDENTIFIED only if best candidate's mean per-glyph distance falls inside the PC3 degraded-self-match band AND beats the runner-up by >=2 sigma over >=20 rune classes.
control_detail: PC1 (quality recovery): 6/6 planted IJG qualities {50,75,85,90,92,95} recovered exactly as singletons by `jpeg_fingerprint.py --selftest`. PC2 (pipeline discrimination): 18 control renders across 9 pipelines x 2 synthetic source PDFs; the fingerprint vector separates Ghostscript's jpeg device (IJG-standard Huffman tables) from ImageMagick (custom/optimised Huffman tables) with no overlap, so the instrument demonstrably can tell renderers apart. PC2b (chain reproduction): `gs -sDEVICE=jpeg -dJPEGQ=92 -r400` followed by ImageMagick at quality 92 reproduces the LP2 vector with BYTE-IDENTICAL DQT tables (luma sha1 c96e442f9ce9a1965c6084df936558fcc335a69f, chroma sha1 cd6e3767d9c4da25c4f8126038b332d0ac48f244), identical marker order for both the colour and the grayscale class, and identical JFIF block. Glyph extraction uses the VALIDATED R9 template-DP reader (96.93% agreement over 5,207 compared glyphs, analysis/retranscribe/diff_report.json), explicitly NOT round12/frontB/forceseg.py which fails its control at 12.9%.

result.encoder_chain: Ghostscript jpeg device (400 dpi, 4:2:0, Artifex sRGB ICC) THEN ImageMagick re-encode at IJG quality 92 with optimised Huffman coding
result.ghostscript_bound: TWO-SIDED, BYTE-EXACT. The LP2 profile's PCS-illuminant bytes (offset 68..79) are 0000f6d5 00010000 0000d32c, md5 e409cef13cd06f6b371f6cddc8e31fcf. Measured against ghostpdl tags: 9.00/9.01/9.02 ship a 3144-byte profile with the canonical illuminant (no match); 9.04, 9.05, 9.06, 9.07, 9.09, 9.10, 9.12, 9.14, 9.15, 9.16, 9.17, 9.18, 9.19, 9.20, 9.21 all ship a 2576-byte profile BYTE-IDENTICAL to the LP2 one; 9.22, 9.26, 9.50, 9.53.3 and 10.06.0 ship the corrected profile (md5 27d2435a749ae91e9974bf7a109a03e5). Artifex introduced the matching profile at 9.04 (2011-08-05) and corrected the two illuminant bytes at 9.22 (2017-10-04). BOUND: Ghostscript >= 9.04 and <= 9.21. Intersected with the artifact's own publication date (onion7, May 2014) the operative window is 9.04-9.14, i.e. 2011-08 to 2014-03. Ubuntu 12.04 LTS shipped Ghostscript 9.05 (2012-02), inside the window and the same distro generation that ships the GnuPG 1.4.11 the author signed with for three years. This also rules out the pages having been re-rendered with any post-2017 Ghostscript.

component_split.note: All 23 grayscale files carry the sRGB (not sGray) profile. Ghostscript's own jpeggray device writes 'Artifex Software sGray ICC Profile'; the observed combination is only produced by a downstream automatic gray detection that passes the source profile through, which is ImageMagick's behaviour.

result.runes_are_typeset: 29/29 rune bitmaps recovered from the page images; uniform nominal height, constant stroke width, flat unserifed terminals, proportional widths 34-64 px. The runes are set from a font, not drawn.
result.platform_corroboration: 46 of 46 curated 3301 PGP-signed messages spanning 2012, 2013 and 2014 carry 'Version: GnuPG v1.4.11 (GNU/Linux)' - a single unchanged GNU/Linux signing environment across three years. GnuPG 1.4.11 was released 2010-10-18 and is the version packaged by Ubuntu 11.04 through 12.04 LTS (Debian wheezy shipped 1.4.12). This string is present in the raw archives but had never been analysed or turned into a finding.

rune_face.metric: D_stretch = 1 - IoU after independent stretch to a common box. The aspect-preserving metric was DISQUALIFIED: every observed bitmap is exactly 114 px tall, which is a height-normalisation artefact of the R9 template pipeline, not a property of the face.

rune_face.verdict: NOT IDENTIFIED, with power. None of the 11 faces is the LP2 rune face: the best candidate sits at 13.6x the measured LP2 reproducibility floor, 4.4x outside the PC3b self-match band, and above the 5th percentile of the wrong-face distribution; separation from the runner-up is 0.23 sigma, i.e. a tie among near-misses. Had the true face been in the bank the instrument would have scored it near 0.03-0.09 (PC3b, 11/11).
rune_face.design_family: Noto Sans Runic and BabelStone Runic - the two modern reference designs of the Anglo-Saxon futhorc - are markedly closer to LP2 (0.41, 0.44) than the wrong-face mean (0.61). All 29 glyph topologies agree, including the variant choices for gyfu, ger, ing and daeg. The divergence is PROPORTION: the LP2 runes are taller and narrower than every candidate, consistent with a condensed face or a non-unit horizontal font-matrix scale - i.e. a typesetting program.

result.local_pdf_scan: No Liber Primus source document present. Every PDF carrying Unicode Runic in its text layer is a derivative document - saved Wikipedia "Anglo-Saxon runes" pages, the 2016 puzzle write-up, and a 2023 academic paper on runic cryptography. No PDF in the local corpus embeds a runic font subset that could be the Liber Primus face.

coverage: All 58 LP2 page JPEGs, every marker, full DQT/DHT/ICC/JFIF/geometry/trailing-byte vector, byte-level. Prior work (corpus/G-forensics) covered pages 0-55 and recorded DQT sha1s only; this lane adds pages 56-57, the exact IJG quality, the Huffman-table classification, the ICC internals and a two-sided release bound, the marker order and the trailing-byte check. 18 control renders across 9 pipelines x 2 source documents, plus 20 two-stage chain runs. 29/29 rune glyph bitmaps via the validated 96.93% reader, matched against 11 Unicode-encoded runic faces under three passing controls. Ghostscript srgb.icc compared byte-exactly across 22 ghostpdl tags from 9.00 to 9.53.3 plus the installed 10.06.0. 46/46 curated 3301 PGP messages checked for signer version. The archived onion7 index.html re-read in full, both copies. 493 distinct locally-held PDFs scanned for a runic text layer or an embedded runic font subset.
